utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any evidence that there were women and children in that column?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some children aged 13, 14. I believe there is one video that shows that, but certainly not appreciable numbers. I mean, there were some isolated incidents, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it reflects the fact that the units are still engaged on task related to the base operations order, and it notes not only the army positions but the MUP is engaged in these activities as well. So, again, on the broader sense, there's a general understanding that at this juncture the 28th Division is now moving in a column formation out of the former enclave and is trying to break out towards Muslim territory. What's not present here, again, is a specific listing of numbers that would give anyone an appreciation to the fact that the size and combat power of the column is far greater than they're estimating at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I left out one part under the situation in the territory. It says: "In the Drina Corps zone of responsibility, the population is being taken from the Srebrenica enclave to Kladanj in an organised manner. It is estimated that on this day, there are about 10.000 Muslims to be transported."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That should be page 3, if they haven't sorted that, on the B/C/S. 4 on the English, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that -- do you have any -- any disagreement with that information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's a reflection of the Drina Corps reporting about the -- the movement of the buses out of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to another report, 65 ter 240.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're still on July 12th, but this document is dated -- it's got a stamp on it or a time on it of about 7.55 p.m., and it's from the Command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, from a person named Captain Pecanac. It reads, "Attention: Major Golic," and it talks a bit about Ramiz Becirovic and Zulfo Tursunovic and some other information about the Muslims. Can you tell us, who is, if you know, Captain Pecanac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Pecanac is an officer from the Main Staff. He works out of the intelligence and security sector. He is often associated by individuals as somebody who is, if not personally responsible for close security for General Mladic, but as an officer who's in charge of coordinating his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. This information that there is a group led by Becirovic and Tursonovic consisting of about 300 men, how accurate do you, in hindsight, as an intelligence, is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's easy to be an intelligence officer in hindsight, but it's a reflection of the fact that the Bratunac Brigade, at this juncture, you know, is getting information related to the column from individuals who they're capturing and questioning, but again reflecting the fact that their numbers are low.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you help with any kind of an estimate of how many -- from what your study of the materials is, how many members of that column made it across that road, the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road, around this time period, 11/12 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the armed front portion of the column, considering the majority of the fighters did, in fact, get across the Konjevic Polje-Milici road that first evening, and I think the numbers generally float around between four and six thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter number 73.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is another State Security document dated 12 July from Dragan Kijac that you have cited in your report as a basis of information and analysis. Unless you have anything special about this -- was this just more information for you in your narrative analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's a reflection of the fact that on the larger level, that there is other information coming out of the enclave that's going into the hands of the Republika Srpska, you know, political leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one, 65 ter 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is, again, from Mr. Kijac on the 12th, providing more information from the area that we're concerned about. Anything particular about this information? I note that at one of the bottom paragraphs, it should be B/C/S page 1, Kijac is saying: "According to the commander of the UNPROFOR Ukrainian Battalion stationed in Zepa, the successful Serbian offensive against Srebrenica caused utter disorientation and uncertainty among the population and the civilian and military authorities of this Muslim enclave." Then he goes on to talk about more facts or more issues related to that, which I don't want to get into. Do you have any idea of the source of where Kijac is getting this information or does this -- can this give you any insight into his sources or anything else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is fairly explicit in identifying the source, that it's the commander of the UNPROFOR Ukrainian Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any idea whether that's a -- whether he's getting that -- how he's getting that from the commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I mean is he -- whether it could be by tapping, overhearing him, or cooperating with him? You have no idea how that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I have no idea how he obtained this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One more of these that you have -- that you've cited. I believe it's 65 ter 75, again 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's from Mr. Kijac, reporting on what's going on in the area on 12 July, reporting on the transportation of the women and children. It reads, looking at the bottom of the English page and the B/C/S page: "When the evacuation was suspended at night and would resume in the morning of the 13th, it should be noted that among the people staying in Potocari, there are hardly any men fit for fighting." Anything -- you want to comment on any of this, aside from just information that assisted you in your evaluation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically. I mean, it's fairly straightforward insomuch as a reflection of the fact that they're receiving information about the composition of the column that could only be obtained from interviewing Bosnian Muslim members of the column who they had captured. It talks about the column itself. It talks about the evacuation. I mean, there's not much interpretation that has to go into it. This is simply a reflection of their reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This kind of document, does it have any value for you as you review all the documents and the facts and try to sort this all out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, as well as the other documents, you know, lay the foundation of what the individuals in the army and what the individuals in the Ministry of the Interior understood the ground truth to be at the time and what they were reporting up their chain of command. So, I mean, from the framework of my analysis and looking at it, you know, how this then impacts what happens in the future, I mean, these are the types of documents that set the framework with respect to who knew what and at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now that we've gone over a few of these State Security reports, do you see any glitches or any -- anything strange or out of the ordinary in the reporting chain and the chain of command in the State Security/Ministry of the interior side of things?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Obviously, some of the information is inaccurate, as one might expect, but this is a reflection of the reporting process working as it should.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter 148, still on 12 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's a time reference to it at 2210 hours on the 12th, as well as a stamp on the 13th from the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade. I'm not sure I need to ask you if this is a time-sensitive document. All right. This is from the Drina Corps Command, Intelligence Section, to the Main Staff, Intelligence and Security Sector, Intelligence Administration of the Drina Corps, Pribicevac, General Krstic personally, General Krstic personally, Drina IKM Bratunac, Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic personally, and the chiefs of intelligence organs, listing the brigades. Does this help us identify anything about the location of Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It identifies that the individual who drafted this report was aware that Colonel Popovic was at the IKM in Bratunac at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Going to the B/C/S page 2, this is -- this is -- I think I failed to mention, but it's from -- it's from Major General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you give an opinion where you believe Tolimir is at this point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that General Tolimir personally would have drafted this report, even though it's under his signature. But it's a reflection of, at this time, General Tolimir is, in fact, at the headquarters of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just calling your attention to - I think we should be able to see most of that - the paragraph on the top of page 2 in the English. I won't read that out, but the first two paragraphs talk about the Muslims in Potocari. Then it says, in the third paragraph: "We have informed organs of the MUP of the RS in Konjevic Polje about the illegal corridor used by the Muslims of Srebrenica, since it is their task to control the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road." What is it you believe General Tolimir is referring to here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated by an earlier document with respect to Dragomir Vasic, the MUP forces were given specific areas of responsibility as part of the larger army programme. What this document does - and, in fact, it notes that the MUP is an addressee of this document, is it reflects that, you know, "We've taken the intelligence report from this particular subject, and we've also taken the next step and we've informed the MUP as to the information on this as well, who are out at the road at Konjevic Polje, because this information could have a direct impact on them." I mean, it shows that, you know, all parties, the MUP and the VRS, are sharing information relevant to the potential military threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I want to read the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just noticed something that I may need some help from the bilingual folks here. It may be an improper translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says: "Brigade commands have the duty to fully inform the SJB in their area of responsibility." Then in English it says: "Intelligence organs shall propose measures to be taken by commands --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Sometimes they get intelligence organs and intelligence and security organs mixed up. I hear silence, so I guess we'll sort that out ourselves, and I'll skip it for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This last paragraph: "The commands of the Bratunac, Zvornik and Milici Brigades, in cooperation with the SJBs in their respective areas of responsibility, shall regulate traffic during the night on the Bratunac-Milici-Vlasenica" and then "Konjevic Polje-Vlasenica roads." This term "cooperation," does this use of cooperation have anything to do with the definition of or the word "cooperation" as you spoke about it a day or two ago when you were going through the JNA rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. In this context, there's not a linkage that they're saying that these local municipal MUP forces are going to be under a form of command of the military for this. This is simply along the lines of, "You need to cooperate with your public safety and security people to ensure that during the evening hours," you know, "the police," you know, "exercise their function and close these roads in part to protect the civilian population, the Bosnian Serb population," so they don't run into a potential combat zone. So I don't look at this, in this context with the local SJBs, as a formal relationship existing between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go back to what I was asking you before, that paragraph in the middle, where it says,"Brigade," because I have been confirmed that this is a correct translation. "Brigade commands have the duty to fully inform the SJB in their area of responsibility. Intelligence organs shall propose measures to be taken by commands to prevent armed Muslims from illegally reaching Tuzla and Kladanj, such as setting up ambushes along the routes they use in order to arrest them and prevent possible surprises against civilians and our combat units along those routes." Can you explain how is it that this would be a job of the intelligence organs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the context of the military threat of the column and the fact that this is a classic intelligence function, what this is saying, essentially, is that intelligence officers in the commands who presumably have the best picture based on the intelligence information they've been receiving need to make sure that, you know, they go to their commanders and their operations people. That's why it's used that general sense phrase "commands," it says, "Let them know where the column is and work with them to propose the best places where the column can be stopped." In this context, the intelligence officers, as a normal function of their duty, would be the most informed about the information that would explain the size of the column and its possible destination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Butler. Mr. President, we're at break time, and I think we're going to finish this week. If we're lucky, we'll finish tomorrow. There's, as you know, in the next days, there's a lot of documents, but we will certainly do our best to get through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of January, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
